title: 7-round AES-256: reported whole-key partial sums, 21 structures

target.description: The authors' reported whole-key attack on 7-round AES-256, with initial whitening and final MixColumns omitted. The detailed filter stage is separately recorded as aes256-7r-integral-fklssww2001-partial-sums; its selected subkey material and the broader whole-cipher claim have different scopes.

setting.key_relation: One unknown master key with the standard AES expansion; no related-key access.
setting.key_population: general secret key; no weak-key restriction reported
setting.plaintext_model: 21 chosen-plaintext structures of 2^32 texts, as tabulated; each varies a four-byte input column.
assumptions: Wrong-subkey rejection uses the paper's heuristic model for zero XOR sums; no numerical whole-procedure success rate is supplied.
The AES-256 schedule supplies the selected round-five equivalent byte but none of the four needed round-six bytes.

This record retains the paper's explicit whole-cipher attack headline. The detailed search first isolates selected subkey material; repeated filtering, reverse expansion or residual search for full master-key completion is not separately costed for every endpoint in this version.

time.note: The paper estimates 2^178 lookups, about 2^170 trial encryptions, per dominating structure; five such structures give its rounded 2^172 total. All 21 structures remain in the data count. This whole-key row preserves the authors' attack-level estimate; it does not infer a new constant factor from the separately catalogued filter.

data.note: Table 1 reports the total filtering structures. The smaller number of structures dominating time does not replace this data requirement. The acquisition budget is the paper's reported attack-level budget.

memory.reported: Partial-sum counter arrays and a 2^32-text structure; peak storage not itemized
memory.note: The section gives intermediate counter sizes and precomputed tables but no complete peak-memory budget for this endpoint.

preprocessing.note: Table preparation and setup are described within the construction but not separately priced for this endpoint.

success.description: No numerical key_recovery success is stated at this exact structure budget. The direct and partial-sums implementations preserve the same aggregate XOR. The 255/256 wrong-key rejection in Section2.1 is for one 256-text Lambda set in the older algorithm; it is not assigned to the improved 2^32-text aggregate or exponentiated over this endpoint. The 19/21-structure AES192/256 extensions use their own key-schedule dependencies. Their source counting and early rejection costs do not quantify all-output success. This is an author full-key headline; numerical success of unitemized completion is not inferred from the selected-subkey relation.

review.scope: Exact-edition endpoint-specific success audit; preserve resource parameters, existing conflicts and full-audit gates. Local source models and conditional relations do not certify whole-output success.

components.description: PDF3–6 Sections2.3–2.4: a correctly hypothesized targeted byte has zero XOR over the complete 2^32-text structure, since it partitions into balanced 256-text sets. Partial sums compute the same XOR exactly; the identity does not imply unique recovery.
